title: Package an MSI for Intune with IntuneWinAppUtil.exe
summary: Turn a vendor MSI into a .intunewin file with separate source and output folders, so the packaging tool never ends up inside its own package.
code:
# Elevated PowerShell, one line. Replace the version folder and MSI name with yours.
& "C:\Packaging\Tools\IntuneWinAppUtil.exe" -c "C:\Packaging\AdminByRequest\8.5.1.0\source" -s "Admin By Request 8.5 Workstation.msi" -o "C:\Packaging\AdminByRequest\8.5.1.0\output" -q

# -c = folder that holds the setup file, -s = the setup file, -o = output folder
# -q  = no prompts, overwrite existing output, create the output folder
# -qq = the same without console output (build pipelines)
notes: 'The folder you specified cannot be accessed' means -c points at the MSI instead of its folder.
Quote every path with spaces and keep the command on one line when you paste it.
